hook: A USCENTCOM special operations mission report (Misrep 9337873) documenting a 20-hour, 1-minute ISR sortie over the Aegean Sea during which a redacted AFSOC crew observed an unidentified, seemingly circular solid object flying just above the ocean surface toward land at an estimated 30 MPH before losing it from their sensor feed.
why_it_matters: This report shows the U.S. military's post-2023 UAP reporting pipeline functioning as designed: a combat ISR crew from 33 SOS filed a structured MISREP through USCENTCOM channels that was formally reviewed and released to AARO. Despite the object remaining unexplained — with propulsion, RF frequency, and advanced capabilities all logged as unknown — the crew's official assessment was 'benign,' illustrating how the institutional framework categorizes low-anomaly UAP encounters. The document's declassification under USCENTCOM MDR 26-0019 and release through the PURSUE program reflects the congressional mandate for systematic UAP disclosure from military archives.
key_findings: UAP was observed at 0811Z on 29 October 2023 by a single AFSOC aircraft (33 SOS / 27 SOW) that was returning to base after a 9-hour-24-minute on-station ISR period; the crew was RTB when the sighting occurred.

The object was formally described in the report as 'seemingly circular, too small to make out details,' flying just above the ocean surface and moving straight toward land — consistent with the war.gov video description of a contrast area tracked by an infrared sensor that became indistinguishable as the background transitioned from water to land.

Estimated kinetic velocity recorded as 30 MPH; both first and last coordinate accuracy are listed as 'estimated,' within a 5-unit radius at grid 35SMV3[redacted], indicating the crew could not precisely fix the object's position.

All formal UAP assessment fields indicate a non-anomalous encounter: physical state = solid; propulsion = unknown; intelligent control = NO; maneuverability observations = none; signatures = none; effects on equipment and persons = none; objects/material recovered = no.

The aircraft carried AGM-114R9E and AGM-114R2 Hellfire missiles and an AN/DAS-4 targeting pod, confirming it was an armed special operations ISR platform; sensors available included G-MESH and FMV/SIGINT collection was the primary mission tasking, with 9:24 FMV hours logged.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document is explicitly stamped 'Approved for Release to AARO' and the UAP section follows AARO's standardized reporting schema, making AARO the direct institutional recipient and custodian of this report.

Declassification under USCENTCOM MDR 26-0019 on 22 January 2026 and release through the PURSUE program reflects the congressional UAP transparency mandates that compelled DoD to systematically declassify and publish military UAP records.
